info.name: ClinicalHarmony · Phase 5b slice 3 — GoldWriter + CMS-0057-F payer API
info.description: GoldWriter (provisional master patients + data lineage; needs docs/db-init/18 and 19 applied) and the CMS-0057-F payer read API served from Gold (GET /fhir/r4/{Coverage,PractitionerRole,MedicationKnowledge,MeasureReport,Device}). Errors on /fhir/r4 are FHIR OperationOutcomes. seed1_patient / seed2_patient are the FHIR ids of Silver seed patients SEED-0001 / SEED-0002 (silver-patient-<silver.patients.id>). Make sure `docker-compose up -d` is running. Run '0b. Auth' first: it does a client_credentials grant against Keycloak (realm clinicalharmony, {{keycloak_url}}) and stores the token in the collection variable access_token, which every request inherits via the collection's Bearer auth (public endpoints ignore it). Tokens live 5 minutes — re-run 0b when you get 401s.

request.description: Expect: 200 OK, body `{"status":"UP"}`. If this fails, the container isn't running — check `docker ps` for clinicalharmony-fhir-compliance-service.

SMART Backend Services-style client_credentials grant (client secret via HTTP Basic). Requests every SMART read scope plus the clinicalharmony/pipeline.write operational scope; the test script stores the token in {{access_token}}, which the collection's Bearer auth sends on every request. Expect: 200 with access_token, token_type Bearer, expires_in 300, and scope echoing what was granted.

item.name: 22. Build one Silver patient → Gold (GoldWriter: master + lineage)

request.description: Expect: 200. Response now includes masterPatientId — the PROVISIONAL 1:1 gold.master_patients row GoldWriter created (first build) or reused (rebuilds) for this Silver patient. In DBeaver: gold.master_patients (match_status = PROVISIONAL), gold.patient_source_xref, and gold.data_lineage (one FHIR_MAP row per resource; transformation_details.steps = SILVER → GOLD with input_hash/output_hash; one PMI_PROVISIONAL row for the master). Run it twice: same masterPatientId, same goldIds, no new lineage rows.

Expect: 200 []. Migration 19 seeds CMS-0057 resources straight into Gold as PENDING_VALIDATION; GoldWriter validates them on startup, so by now nothing is pending. To see it work: UPDATE gold.fhir_resources SET compliance_notes = '{"status":"PENDING_VALIDATION","seed":"19_seed_cms0057_gold.sql"}' WHERE fhir_id = 'cms-practitionerrole-2'; then re-send — one summary back, usCoreCompliant false, rule pd-1.
Expect: 200 searchset Bundle, total 1 (SEED-0001's commercial PPO Coverage). Validated against us-core-coverage.
Expect: 200 application/fhir+json. Response headers: X-Profile-Compliant: true, X-Validated-Profile: us-core-coverage, ETag, Last-Modified.
Expect: 200, total 2. Try also ?active=true&specialty=207Q00000X (AND) → 1, or ?role=207Q00000X,207RC0000X (comma = OR) → 2.
Expect: 200 with X-Profile-Compliant: false. Deliberately seeded with no telecom and no endpoint → US Core pd-1. The reasons are in gold.fhir_resources.compliance_notes.
Expect: 200, total 1 (metformin 500 MG Oral Tablet, SCD + its SCDG). Validated against Da Vinci US Drug Formulary 2.1.0 usdf-FormularyDrug. Try ?status=active&_count=2 → total 3, 2 entries.

Expect: 200, total 1. An unversioned canonical matches any version (the stored one is pinned |0.1.000, as DEQM's deqm-0 requires). Validated against Da Vinci DEQM 5.0.0 indv-measurereport-deqm. Also: ?patient={{seed1_patient}}.

item.name: 30. CMS-0057 — Device by patient and SNOMED type

request.description: Expect: 200, total 1 (SEED-0002's pacemaker). Validated against us-core-implantable-device.
Expect: 404, OperationOutcome issue code not-supported, listing the 5 supported types.
Expect: 400, OperationOutcome issue code invalid, naming the parameter and listing the supported ones. Strict handling: an ignored filter would return more data than asked for.
Expect: 400 (modifiers not supported). Also try ?patient=Practitioner/cms-practitioner-1 (wrong reference type), ?_count=1000 (cap 100), PractitionerRole?active=yes.
Expect: 200 and the X-Correlation-Id you sent echoed back in the response headers (and stamped on this request's log lines).
